title: Studio scripting
blurb: Actions, branches, API actions, and a lab canvas that does not pretend to be an import file.

lessons.title: Script types and the POC contract
lessons.summary: You create a script for a media type. Phone scripts serve phone POCs. One digital script type serves digital channels. The POC selects exactly one.

p: A script is created for a media type. The POC is assigned one script, and that script must define the flow from the start of the interaction. The default skill comes from the POC and the script may replace it.
Digital Channels says the digital script type covers all digital channels, with differences a scripter still has to learn. Other script types are for legacy ACD channels.

Develop a Basic Script starts an inbound phone script with the actions that verify someone can help, play a menu, request an agent, and play music. The setup page names BEGIN and REQAGENT as the first pair to connect.
A digital POC should not be given that phone script. The media types differ.

lessons.title: BEGIN, MENU, REQAGENT, MUSIC, WAIT
lessons.summary: The basic tutorial is a menu, a skill request per branch, and music until answer. The Classics bullseye insert is Music for 90 seconds and then UpdateContact.

p: Menu plays a prompt, prerecorded, TTS, or both, and stores the contact's entry in the variable you name. The sample is sales, support, and billing. The digit selects the branch.
The tutorial tells you to set each Reqagent's skill to the inbound phone skill for that destination, assigned to the agents who do that work.
Music and Wait hold the contact until answer. In the Classics bullseye story, Music is 90 seconds and UpdateContact widens proficiency from 1–5 to 1–8.
Reqagent can carry the opening window. UpdateContact carries the next one. Both are on the bullseye action list with COUNTAGENTS and GETQUEUE.

lessons.title: API actions are not help pages
lessons.summary: API actions call CXone REST APIs from Studio. They are not documented as action help. Use the developer portal. Not every API has an action.
objectives: Find them on the API palette
Open the portal, not a missing help page

p: API actions sit on the API Actions palette. POST is green, PUT orange, GET blue, DEL red, PATCH aqua. Security-related actions show a purple shield. Categories match the developer portal.
They do not have online help pages. Not every API has an action. The REST API action or a Snippet is how you call the rest. The page mentions Snippet as a traditional method beside the action.

sections.h: GET NEXT EVENT as a specimen
p: The GET NEXT EVENT help page is an exception that exists because it is documented as an API action: it polls the agent event queue. It points you at the get-next-event agent sessions API on the developer portal.
That page says the call is typically for building an agent application. It is not a general routing action.

lessons.title: Trace the contact, not the picture
lessons.summary: A script picture can be wrong in three cited ways: the POC points elsewhere, Reqagent skill is blank, or the proficiency window excludes the idle agents. Trace those before you trace packets.
objectives: Check the window against real proficiencies

p: First confirm the point of contact names this script. Second confirm each Reqagent names the skill you think, because blank means the POC skill. Third compare High and Low with the agents' proficiencies, remembering 1 is best.
The builder in this lab validates a single BEGIN, a non-empty skill warning, a menu with at least two branches, and a window inside 1–20 with high less than or equal to low.
This lab does not have a copy of Studio's trace tool and does not invent its buttons. Use the product's trace when you have a tenant. Use the three checks when you are still on paper.
API action failures belong to the portal: token, permission on the role, and the tenant's api_endpoint.

lessons.title: Digital scripts
lessons.summary: Digital scripts plus digital skills are the preferred inbound method. Workflow automation can run beside them. Update Contact Digital does not accelerate priority.
objectives: Prefer the skill and the script
Keep WFA as a partner, not a substitute you forget
Use the digital update action's rules

p: Digital Routing says Studio and workflow automation work together. WFA rules run independent of scripts. You can use both. New inbound configuration is skills and scripts. Outbound still uses routing queues.
Sub-skills tied to queues are not the recommended method. The manage-digital-skills page says Studio is the recommended way to assign skills.

Update Contact Digital changes priority and proficiency range to widen the pool. Priority is 0–1000 and does not accelerate. High and low proficiency are 1–20. Default routing criteria is Not Applicable.
TextBot Exchange, when a virtual agent is in the digital script, is a different action. Do not confuse it with a routing update.

lessons.title: Virtual hold, as the product page states it
lessons.summary: The Studio integration page says virtual hold can disconnect the caller and create a callback when an agent is free, so the caller does not wait on the line. It does not list the action's properties there.

figure.caption: Stay on the line, or leave

p: NiCE CXone Studio, on the integrations page, says advanced actions include Estimated Wait Time and Virtual Hold. Virtual hold is the ability to disconnect and create a callback that runs when an agent is available, avoiding a long wait on the line.
Estimated wait time is named in the same sentence as a way to fine-tune routing. The page does not give the action's fields.
You can write the experience: offer a callback instead of Music. You cannot, from this page, write the property names, the callback caller-id rules, or the reporting columns.
Music remains the documented 'stay on the line' treatment in the basic tutorial.
